memory_candidates.content: When two macro/notation tokens must SWAP meanings (A's old rendering becomes B's, B's old rendering becomes A's) across a large prose document, do it as a two-step word-boundary sed in a fixed order: first rename every A-token to a fresh third name C (A -> C), THEN rename every B-token to A (B -> A). Never try A -> B and B -> A in either order directly, or in parallel -- both orderings either merge the two token sets or require lookahead/lookbehind regex that is fragile across sed dialects. Verify with occurrence counts before and after each step, not just after the whole swap.

A #leansrc("Module.Path", "decl")-style citation macro in a typst document needs TWO independent checks, not one: (1) does the module resolve to a real file (or, for an aggregator-style citation, a real directory subtree)? and (2) does that exact decl name appear there as an actual Lean declaration (theorem|lemma|def|structure|inductive|abbrev|class|instance NAME), not merely as a substring inside a docstring or comment that happens to mention the name? A naive substring grep against the cited file produces false negatives when the decl is namespaced (e.g. `theorem Foo.bar` vs. citing bare `bar`) and false positives when the identifier is only ever discussed in prose, never actually declared (a sign the theorem was renamed and the citation went stale).

In this repository's FormalSystem/ tree, an aggregator .lean file (one that only imports submodule files, e.g. Metalogic/WeakCanonical.lean) is a legitimate #leansrc citation target for a declaration that actually lives in one of its submodules -- this is NOT staleness. Genuine staleness is when the declaration lives in a completely different top-level file or directory subtree than the one cited (e.g. citing Metalogic.BXCanonical for a theorem that was later moved to the sibling file Metalogic/StrongCompleteness.lean). When auditing #leansrc citations, scope the existence check to the cited module's own directory subtree before concluding a citation is stale.
